scenes.headline: One hacked IT tool. Many hacked companies.
scenes.say: Small businesses: your IT provider could be the way in. Here is how one hacked management tool can reach every computer it looks after.

scenes.headline: One console to run many companies' computers
scenes.body: Remote monitoring and management: deploy software, run scripts, open remote sessions
scenes.say: Many IT providers use remote monitoring and management tools, called RMM. From one console they deploy software, run scripts and open remote sessions on computers across many companies.

scenes.headline: Run code on the server without logging in
scenes.say: A real example is N-able N-central. In September, N-able fixed CVE-2026-86218, a critical flaw that let attackers run code on the N-central server without logging in.

scenes.headline: From break-in to emergency deadline
scenes.source: The Hacker News · Field Effect · Canadian Cyber Centre
scenes.say: On September fourth, the security firm Huntress investigated a break-in at one customer's N-central server. On the fifth, N-able shipped Hotfix 4. On the eighth, the US agency CISA listed the flaw as exploited, and gave federal agencies until the eleventh to patch.

scenes.headline: Which flaw was used? Unconfirmed.
scenes.body: Huntress says limited logging means it cannot confirm the exploit. N-able later said the flaw was exploited in the wild.
scenes.source: The Hacker News · Canadian Cyber Centre
scenes.say: Huntress says limited logging means it cannot confirm which flaw was used in that break-in. N-able later told customers the flaw has been exploited in the wild.

scenes.headline: Compromise N-central, and you gain access to all connected computers and downstream systems.
scenes.say: Researchers at watchTowr, who reproduced the flaw, put it simply: compromise N-central, and you gain access to all connected computers and downstream systems.

scenes.headline: N-central security flaws patched in five weeks
scenes.say: And it was not a one-off. Between August second and September fifth, N-able patched five N-central security flaws across four hotfixes.

scenes.headline: Update to 2026.3 Hotfix 4 or later
scenes.body: Self-hosted servers need the update; N-able says its hosted customers were already patched
scenes.say: If your company runs N-central on its own servers, update to 2026.3 Hotfix 4 or later. N-able says its hosted customers were already patched.

scenes.headline: Your security is partly your provider's security.
scenes.body: The tool that can touch every computer deserves the strongest locks.
scenes.say: Analyst note: your security is partly your provider's security. The tool that can touch every computer deserves the strongest locks, and you are allowed to ask about them.

scenes.headline: Four questions for your IT provider
items: Is your management tool patched, and how fast?
Is its login hidden from the open internet?
Would you notice a new admin account?
Do you review its logs and remote sessions?
scenes.say: Four questions for your IT provider. Is your management tool patched, and how fast? Is its login hidden from the open internet? Would you notice a new admin account? And do you review its logs and remote sessions?
